note: Transferable skill categories that business analyst job-posting phrases map to. A category names a skill, never a product: tools are listed below and point at the skill they are used for. Seeded from the IIBA BABOK knowledge areas and the 36 concepts of the first business analyst course; new categories are proposed from real postings.

categories.name: Business analysis practice
categories.description: the discipline itself: business analysis methods, planning the analysis work, BABOK-style techniques, being the link between business and delivery

categories.name: Stakeholder management
categories.description: identifying, engaging and communicating with stakeholders, managing expectations and relationships

categories.name: Requirements elicitation
categories.description: finding out what the business needs: interviews, workshops, observation, surveys, gathering requirements

categories.name: Requirements analysis and documentation
categories.description: analysing, specifying and documenting requirements: user stories, business and functional requirements, specifications, traceability, process and solution documentation

categories.name: Process modeling and improvement
categories.description: mapping current and future-state processes (flowcharts, BPMN), analysing them and proposing process or system improvements

categories.name: Root cause analysis and problem solving
categories.description: finding the cause of problems and issues, critical and analytical thinking, troubleshooting, diagnosing data or system issues

categories.name: Data analysis and statistics
categories.description: analysing data to support decisions: statistical analysis, forecasting, hypothesis testing, quantitative and analytical modelling

categories.name: SQL and data querying
categories.description: writing queries to read and shape data in relational databases

categories.name: Data mapping and integration
categories.description: source-to-target mappings, data migration and integration requirements, data definitions and lineage

categories.name: Reporting, KPIs and dashboards
categories.description: defining and maintaining KPIs and recurring reports, building dashboards and data visualisations

categories.name: Spreadsheet analysis
categories.description: analysis and modelling in spreadsheets: formulas, pivot tables, lookups

categories.name: Testing and user acceptance
categories.description: test cases and scenarios, user acceptance testing, regression testing, defect tracking and resolution, QA

categories.name: Change management and adoption
categories.description: change control and change requests, organisational change, user training and adoption

categories.name: Agile delivery and backlog management
categories.description: agile and scrum ways of working, backlog and sprint management, product ownership at team level

categories.name: Project coordination and reporting
categories.description: tracking project status, timelines and tasks, reporting progress, coordinating delivery across teams

categories.name: Prioritization and trade-offs
categories.description: prioritising work and requirements, weighing trade-offs, recommending execution paths

categories.name: Communication and presentation
categories.description: written and verbal communication, presenting findings, demonstrating solutions and building slide decks

categories.name: Cross-functional collaboration
categories.description: working across teams and functions, teamwork, collaborating with technical and business groups

categories.name: Enterprise systems analysis
categories.description: analysing, configuring, testing, upgrading and supporting business systems such as ERP, HR, finance, student and lending platforms

categories.name: Compliance, controls and risk
categories.description: regulatory compliance, internal controls, audit support, risk and governance requirements

categories.name: Business case and financial analysis
categories.description: costing, pricing and credit/market analysis, ROI and business cases that support funding and pricing decisions

categories.name: AI-assisted analysis
categories.description: using AI tools in analysis work: prompting, checking AI output, summarising and drafting with AI, understanding AI features and their limits

categories.name: Industry and domain knowledge
categories.description: knowing the industry or business function the work sits in, with its rules, vocabulary and standards: healthcare billing and coding, banking and credit, insurance claims, revenue cycle, sector regulation, and functional domains such as treasury and cash management, payments and payment standards (ISO 20022), and HR functions (compensation and benefits, talent and performance management, offboarding)

categories.name: Programming and scripting for analysis
categories.description: writing code in a scripting or general-purpose language to clean, analyse, automate and report on data: Python, R, Visual Basic (VBA) and general programming for analysis work. Not platform or infrastructure engineering (big-data platforms, operating systems, directory services) and not building software products

examples.phrase: prepare executive presentations and board materials
use BI tools to visualize data insights for stakeholders
map current-state and future-state finance processes
write acceptance criteria for new features
identify data quality issues and propose fixes
configure SAP modules to meet functional requirements
